subject: how to provide site-occasion level covariates for communityModel function

messages.author: 7eed7eee7dd92cf3
messages.subject: how to provide site-occasion level covariates for communityModel function
parts:
Hi again,

my last question is: 

how is possible to provide site-occasion level covariates for the communityModel function?

The detections cover a window time of 3186 days, the matrix calculated by the function camOp has 2958 occasions, and the active nights are only 282.

I have a site-occasion level covariate (number of days since the first day of each year) which should be provided within the slot obsCovs of the data_list, but how?

I thought to use the DetHist_list[[1]]effort and substituting the effort with the values calculated for each detection, but the dimensions are not equal. 

A workaround might be to save the matrix effort as .csv file and then manually input the values for each occasion and each site, but of course this solution is not ideal. 

Any suggestions? 

Stef

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] how to provide site-occasion level covariates for communityModel function
parts:
Hi,
Is this your non-camera trapping data set again? Normally if your survey covers 3186 days then the camera operation matrix should have 3186 columns, one for each day without gaps. That is the case even if there are only 282 active days. *

You said:
I thought to use the DetHist_list[[1]]effort and substituting the effort with the values calculated for each detection, but the dimensions are not equal.

The solution should be something along those lines. It should actually work if occasionLength = 1. With longer occasions you can maybe start with the camera operation matrix and replace the values with the days since the start of the year. On the other hand if you have occasions or 2 or more days then you may end up with occasions that cover the old and new year, and averaging the number of days since the year began doesn't make sense.
Also, "the dimensions are not equal" is not very helpful without seeing the code you used and the dimensions of the object you created.

Anyways, I'd suggest to first check that the cam op matrix is correct and has no gaps.

* This may not be ideal or necessary from a data management perspective, but that's how it is currently.

Best,
Jürgen

Hi Jurgen, 

yes it is that dataset and I confirm that the dimensions of the DetHist_list[[1]]$effort are not equal to the dimensions of the camera operation matrix. 
Note that camtrapR functions are not raising warnings. I was expecting to get an effort matrix equal to the camera operation matrix, but may be I am wrong on this expectation. 

Stef

#loading data
mydet <- read.csv("/Users/stefanoanile/Desktop/Dragonflies in Sicily/Truncated_Dataset/mydet.trunc_2023_07_23.csv",header=TRUE,sep=",")
camera.operation.trunc <- read_ods("/Users/stefanoanile/Desktop/Dragonflies in Sicily/Truncated_Dataset/camera.table.trunc.ods",sheet=1,col_names=TRUE)

cam.op.trunc <- cameraOperation(CTtable=camera.operation.trunc,stationCol="idsite",setupCol="start.time",retrievalCol="end.time",hasProblems=TRUE,dateFormat="y-m-d")

report.trunc<-surveyReport (recordTable=mydet,CTtable=camera.operation.trunc,camOp=cam.op.trunc,speciesCol = "species",stationCol="idsite",cameraCol="idsite",setupCol="start.time",retrievalCol="end.time",CTDateFormat ="%Y-%m-%d",recordDateTimeCol = "datetime",recordDateTimeFormat = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")

#inspecting objects#
#str(cam.op.trunc)#
#  num [1:80, 1:3187] NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA ...
#  - attr(*, "dimnames")=List of 2
#   ..$ : chr [1:80] "Alcara li Fusi Fiumara di Rosmarino" "Ali Torrente Ali ponte" "Bronte Laghetto Case Rosse" "Buseto Palizzolo Rio Forgia alto" ...
#   ..$ : chr [1:3187] "2014-10-04" "2014-10-05" "2014-10-06" "2014-10-07" ...

min.date <- min(ymd(substr(mydet$datetime,1,10)))
# [1] "2014-10-05 11:00:00"
max.date <- max(ymd(substr(mydet$datetime,1,10)))
# [1] "2023-06-25 11:00:00"
tdf <- max.date-min.date
# Time difference of 3185 days
mysimulate.days <- seq(min.date,max.date,by=1)

#checking length
length(mysimulate.days)
# [1] 3186

#creating detection matrix#
DetHist_list <- lapply(unique(mydet$species), FUN = function(x) {
   detectionHistory(
     recordTable         = mydet,
     camOp                = cam.op.trunc,
     stationCol           = "idsite",
     speciesCol           = "species",
     recordDateTimeCol    = "datetime",
     species              = x,     # this gets modifies by lapply
     occasionLength       = 1,
     day1                 = "station",
     datesAsOccasionNames = TRUE,
     includeEffort        = TRUE,
     scaleEffort          = FALSE,
     timeZone             = "Europe/Rome"
   )}
 )

dim.effort <- str(DetHist_list[[1]]$effort)
# str(DetHist_list[[1]]$effort)
#  num [1:80, 1:2958] 0.5 0.5 0.5 0.5 0.5 0.5 0.5 0.5 0.5 0.5 ...
#  - attr(*, "dimnames")=List of 2
#   ..$ : chr [1:80] "Alcara li Fusi Fiumara di Rosmarino" "Ali Torrente Ali ponte" "Bronte Laghetto Case Rosse" "Buseto Palizzolo Rio Forgia alto" ...
#   ..$ : chr [1:2958] "day1_day1" "day2_day2" "day3_day3" "day4_day4" ...

Does that solve the problem?

Best,
Jürgen
